title: Fiber Internet in Seattle: Quantum, AT&T, Astound, Ziply
description: Fiber internet in Seattle: who offers it in each of 41 ZIP codes, Quantum Fiber and AT&T Fiber prices, Astound and Ziply coverage, and what to check first.
lead: Who offers fiber in Seattle, how widely, what it costs now that Quantum Fiber belongs to AT&T, and how to confirm it at your address.
short_answer: Quantum Fiber, now owned by AT&T, is Seattle's main fiber provider and reports service in all 41 Seattle ZIP codes we track, with symmetrical plans up to 8 Gbps. Astound has fiber in parts of 22 ZIP codes, usually a small or partial share of each. Ziply Fiber reaches only the north edge of the city. Fiber in a ZIP code does not mean fiber on every street.

sections.h2: Quantum Fiber is now part of AT&T
sections.body_html: AT&T bought Lumen's consumer fiber business, including Quantum Fiber, for $5.75 billion. The deal closed on February 2, 2026, and AT&T named Seattle among the major metro areas it gained. As of mid-2026 AT&T was still moving customers market by market, so you will see both a Quantum Fiber page and an AT&T Fiber page for Seattle, with different prices. Quantum Fiber tells existing customers their plan, speed and unlimited data are unchanged for now, and that AT&T terms apply 30 days after they are notified.

Prices as shown on November 25, 2026. Quantum's prices include a $5 discount for bank-account autopay plus paperless billing, and its 1, 2 and 3 Gig prices also include new-customer savings of $25 to $30 a month (1 Gig is $75 before savings); taxes and fees are extra, and no price lock or end date for the savings is stated. AT&T's prices include an autopay discount, are plus taxes and fees, and installation can cost up to $99. Both say there is no annual contract. Since the same network sits behind both brands, check both at your address and take the lower price in writing.

sections.h2: Astound, Ziply and the cable alternative
sections.body_html:
1. Astound: serves Washington homes by coaxial cable or fiber depending on location. Its Washington page lists 300 Mbps from $30 a month for 12 months, but with a 400 GB data allowance on that plan; data is unlimited on 1 Gig and up.
  2. Ziply Fiber: based in Kirkland and bought by Canada's BCE in August 2025. In Seattle it only reaches the north edge of the city, mainly 98177.
  3. Xfinity: reports cable in all 41 ZIP codes with up to 2 Gbps both ways in our data. Its Seattle page listed 300 Mbps at $45 a month with a 5-year price guarantee on November 25, 2026, with autopay from a bank account and paperless billing, for new customers (offer listed as ending November 30).

Check three things: whether fiber reaches your building, not just your ZIP code; the price in month 13; and, for apartments, whether your building has its own provider deal. See the full list of Seattle internet providers, compare with fiber in Phoenix, or test your current speed first. All Washington providers are at internet in Washington.

faq: Yes. Quantum Fiber, now owned by AT&T, reports fiber in all 41 Seattle ZIP codes we track, but coverage within each ZIP code is partial, so check your address.
Is Quantum Fiber now AT&T Fiber in Seattle?
AT&T completed its purchase of Lumen's consumer fiber business, including Quantum Fiber, on February 2, 2026. Both brand names were still in use in Seattle in late 2026.
What is the fastest internet in Seattle?
Quantum Fiber lists an 8 Gig symmetrical plan in limited areas. Ziply Fiber reports up to 6 Gbps in a few north Seattle ZIP codes.
Is Astound fiber or cable in Seattle?
Both. Astound reports fiber in parts of 22 Seattle ZIP codes and cable in 21, and says the connection depends on location.
Is Ziply Fiber available in Seattle?
Only on the north edge of the city. Ziply reports fiber in 3 of 41 Seattle ZIP codes, mainly 98177.
